Objectifs : Concevoir un ensemble de log:
Objectives: Design an inclusive collective housing complex (student flatshares, intergenerational housing or emergency accommodation) on the historic site of the former Hôpital de La Rochefoucauld in Paris's 14th arrondissement. The project develops combinable 150 m² "dwelling units" for five to six residents, balancing community life with individual privacy. Set along a narrow buildable strip beside a sloping lane, the repeated architecture forms a porous threshold between the street and a new public park. The design explores the interplay of solid and void, the relationship to the ground and the outdoor spaces, while extending the site's social purpose.

Concept: Organise the project around a rigid square grid and a central, triple-height courtyard. Suspended walkways connect and serve the student apartments. Each identical square-plan unit has a private loggia. The deep facade integrates bespoke furniture (tables, benches and planters) as well as removable curtains that each student can customise.

Duration: 4 weeks

Grade: 17/20 (highest grade)
Objectifs : Concevoir une maison-atelier:
Objectives: Design an urban live-work studio in Ivry-sur-Seine, combining a 125 m² workspace and exhibition area with an 80 m², three-room home on a narrow 7.5 × 17 m plot. Key architectural devices—including a double-height space, a courtyard and carefully controlled natural light—shape the spaces and their atmosphere. The project stages the transition between work and home through its volumes, framed views, considered uses and the display of artworks in the showroom.

Concept: Create a studio for a glass artisan, with a ground-floor exhibition gallery and a lower-level workshop with double-height space. The home occupies the upper floors as a through-apartment duplex, with views down into the studio and two bedrooms on the top floor. The thick-facade concept is developed through broad vertical elements that incorporate loggias, terraces, seating and indoor/outdoor shelves.

Duration: 3 weeks

Grade: 18/20 (highest grade)
Objectifs : Concevoir l'analyse et la re:
Objectives: Analyse and produce a complete graphic record of a notable building featured in Éric Lapierre's Guide d'architecture Paris 1900–2008. Through archival research and on-site surveys, the project examines the building's spatial, structural and technical aspects. The work documents it through measured drawings (plans, sections and elevations), a study model, and architectural hypotheses for undocumented elements.

Concept: Spatial and structural analysis of the mixed-use complex comprising Saint-Luc Church and its residential building. The study highlights how the church's cultural and sacred programme coexists with residential use within the same structure.

Duration: 3 weeks

Grade: 15/20 (highest grade)
Objectifs : Concevoir une extension cont:
Objectives: Design a contemporary rooftop home above an existing building in the historic Butte-Rouge garden city in Châtenay-Malabry. The project begins with paired observation and on-site drawing to understand the neighbourhood, its history and architecture. It studies the transition from the street to private domestic space, then proposes a modern home that sits above the existing building while respecting its natural and heritage setting.

Concept: Analyse the existing building and develop the interior through the composition of the facades and openings. The project creates a duplex for a family with five children, surrounded by terraces that extend the living spaces outdoors.

Duration: 3 weeks

Grade: 15/20 (highest grade)
Objectif : Concevoir une halle couverte:
Objective: Design a covered hall of less than 300 m² (a covered market or a shelter for swimmers) on Place de Stalingrad, facing the Rotonde de Stalingrad, the former toll gate designed by Claude Nicolas Ledoux. The project explores covering and structure in a dense urban setting shaped by the Bassin de la Villette, the elevated metro and heavy pedestrian flows. Through levels, access and permeability, it develops a strong siting strategy—balancing presence and disappearance—and brings the new building into dialogue with the historic Rotonde.

Concept: Use two large pitched roofs to create generous interior volumes suited to a hall. A broad suspended walkway connects the structures and their rooftops, which become terraces and dining areas overlooking the site.

Duration: 4 weeks

Objectifs : Concevoir un module de logem:
Objectives: Design a repeatable student-housing module conceived as a large inhabited window, with sleeping, cooking, working, washing and storage functions integrated along the facade. Based on precise dimensions (5 × 3.7 m and 5 m high) and facing one direction, the project explores architecture from the inside out. It develops a bespoke envelope through framed views, natural light, summer comfort and insulation, giving each use its own spatial quality.

Concept: Create a two-storey home with a setback that forms a terrace. A large glazed facade accommodates all the functions and plays with the visual balance of solid and void, as if a substantial volume were suspended above empty space. The thick facade becomes inhabited space, integrating furniture and everyday uses.

Duration: 3 weeks

Grade: 16/20 (highest grade in the group)
Objectifs : Concevoir un pavillon de ser:
Objectives: Design a service pavilion for sustainable mobility in the heart of Parc des Grands-Moulins, as a meeting point for cyclists. Across two levels, it combines indoor and outdoor spaces: a repair workshop, shelter for 25 bicycles, offices and an elevated terrace. The design explores timber structure, using the grid, member dimensions and material thickness to ensure stability and give the building a distinct identity.

Concept: Connect the different levels of the park and avenue. Stepped stairs provide storage and outdoor terraces. On the ground floor, the bicycle garage arranges functions from public to private along the depth of the building, while openings beneath the stairs create visual links between the two floors.

Duration: 3 weeks

Grade: 15/20 (highest grade: 17/20)
Objectif : Concevoir une micro-architect:
Objective: Design a plaster micro-architecture based on a simple geometric form (square, circle or diagonal) to organise three basic functions: sleeping, washing and eating. The project is carved from a solid mass, with no roof, doors, windows or added furniture. The table, bed and shower are formed directly from the floor and walls. The space follows the sun's path to work with natural light and wall height. The final design is made as a negative mould so it can be cast as one piece.

Concept: Imagine a semicircular room whose spaces and openings follow the curve of its geometry. A thick wall integrates the kitchen, bathroom and bedroom. Changes in level and a series of steps emphasise depth and the perception of volume.

Duration: 1 week

Aeris est une équipe de cinq membres du:
Aeris is a five-member team from Jean Mermoz High School in Saint-Louis. After winning the French national finals, the team qualified for the 2025 STEM Racing World Finals in Singapore.

The project covers every aspect of a business: engineering (Onshape CAD design, CFD simulations, mass optimisation and five-axis machining at ISL), project management (ClickUp, a RACI matrix and a €30,000 budget), marketing, social media, sponsor outreach and sustainability.

The Aeris car weighs approximately 48.3 g and uses Kanzen ceramic-hybrid bearings and 7075 aluminium wheels. A MATLAB/Simulink model estimates a track time of 1.067 seconds over 24 metres.
